beats.say: The cloud is handy: files open from anywhere. But a link shared the wrong way also opens from anywhere.
When you create a link, check three things: who can open it, whether they can edit, and until when it stays open.
Sometimes there is no password at all, just allow the app. One tap can hand the attacker a key to your account.

subject.text: Leyla Guliyeva shared a document with you

body.text: To open it, allow the DocuSfera Viewer app to access your account.

beats.say: If you allowed it, changing your password may not be enough. Ask technical support to revoke the app at once.

scenes.prompt: Find what this app asks for beyond its job.

label.text: See your name and email address
Read, send and delete your emails
Full access to all your files
Keep access even when you are not using it

spots.label: Full mailbox access
spots.explain: Merging PDFs does not need your mail. With this, someone can send emails in your name.

spots.label: All files
spots.explain: The app needs only the file you pick, not your whole cloud.

spots.label: Contacts
spots.explain: Your contact list becomes the target list for the next phishing wave.

spots.label: Standing access
spots.explain: The app can keep getting in after you leave. Changing your password does not always cut this off.

question.prompt: You send a report to two colleagues to read. Which link?

options.label: Anyone with the link, can edit
options.feedback: If the link leaks, anyone can open and change the file.

options.label: Only the two colleagues, view only, with an expiry date
Everyone in the organisation, can edit
options.feedback: Hundreds of people who do not need it could open and change it.

scenes.explain: Give the least access: named people, only the rights they need, and an end date.

scenes.prompt: Is this share safe or risky?

subject.text: Samir Babayev shared the file Quarterly report with you

body.text: Samir: here is the report we discussed yesterday.

cards.explain: A known colleague, an expected file, the service's own domain. Still check the address bar when it opens.

subject.text: 3 files sent to you: Salary increase 2027.pdf

body.text: Files will be deleted in 24 hours. Confirm your email password to view them.

cards.explain: Wrong domain, a tempting topic, time pressure and a password request. A classic trap.
This link lets anyone edit. Change the access level before you send it.

body.text: I uploaded the documents to my personal cloud so I can work from home.

cards.explain: A personal cloud is outside your organisation's control. Keep work files only in the approved service.

subject.text: Old open links will be closed

body.text: On Friday, open links older than 90 days will close automatically. No action is needed from you.

cards.explain: Correct address, no link, no request. This is a useful clean-up.

scenes.prompt: Match each access level to what it means.
scenes.explain: Edit rights nobody needs raise the risk of mistakes or harmful changes.

points: Share links with named people and only the rights needed.
Never let an unknown app into your account.
Keep work files out of personal clouds.
